mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% for two consecutive months predicts a forward discounting effect that lowers the present value of expected equity cash flows, driving negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains >2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not sustain the level for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE over the next month signals labor market strengthening without wage inflation, which reduces real wage growth and dampens equity valuations, producing a negative 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% YoY while UNRATE decreases by >0.1pp in the following month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening without wage pressure
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during similar labor market transitions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST above 600 signals accelerating demand for consumer goods, which lowers the cost of capital via higher equity valuation multiples, yielding a positive 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during periods of rising HOUST without other macro shifts.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO below 92 coincides with elevated GDPC1, indicating supply-side contraction that raises uncertainty and compresses forward discounting, resulting in a negative 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% from previous month while GDPC1 rises by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or indistinguishable from zero during similar contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS falls below 1% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the lower discount rate increases the present value of expected equities, producing a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for three consecutive months and macro regime is non-recessionary
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in UNRATE above 10% followed by a decline in PAYEMS suggests rising labor market friction and potential wage stagnation, which reduces equity risk appetite and drives a negative 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in a single month while PAYEMS decreases by >1% in the next month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive and statistically significant during analogous UNRATE spikes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both HOUST and RSAFS of at least 10% indicate weakening demand across sectors, which elevates idiosyncratic risk and compresses forward pricing, producing a negative 20-day return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < prev_month -10% and RSAFS < prev_month -10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during comparable contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO above 95 while CPIAUCSL remains flat suggests robust supply expansion without price pressures, lowering real interest rates and supporting positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) during sustained supply expansion.
